The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 11b3a102e7333bf8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 15-16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let 0 < ζ < 1, let E > 0, and set δ = E/8, a0 = 10−6 ζδ, q = ζδ/20, ρ0 = ζδ/1000, M = ⌈15/ζ⌉ + 3, N = 6(M + 1). (6) 15 Suppose 0 < a ≤ a0, and let p : Y → R be (1 − ζ)-Lipschitz for dJ . There is a random function Q : Y → R, obtained using finitely many independent scalar noises uniform on [q, 2q], with the following properties. 1. For every realization, Q respects all switches, is 1-Lipschitz for dJ , and satisfies |Q(v)−p(v)| ≤ 6δ < E. 2. Its pieces use finitely many named atoms of the form A(v) = C + εdJ (k, v), ε ∈ {−1, 1}, k ∈ Y. (7) Each name specifies a source k and sign ε fixed before the noises are sampled; the intercept C is random. Whenever the construction reuses an atom, it retains its name. 3. For a fixed x ∈ Y and 0 < ρ ≤ ρ0, there is a list A(x, ρ) of at most N atom names and sources, determined without the noises, that contains the name of every atom selected by Q on BdJ (x, ρ). Except on an event of probability at most N2 q (8ρ + η), (8) one named atom is selected throughout this ball. Here η = 0 for continuous uniform noises. Alternatively, each noise may be uniform on an equally spaced grid including both endpoints of [q, 2q], and η in (8) may be the largest grid spacing. The same conclusions hold for any set of points reached from x by band paths of length at most ρ, including the points and representatives encountered on those paths.
